outcome: No event since 26 January 2024 settles or moves this bullet. The only in-window paper on Todorcevic's OCA (Notaro, arXiv:2601.01166, 3 Jan 2026) answers a question about Baumgartner's Axiom and says nothing about the continuum. The latest source I could read that states the status of the bullet's question (the Gilton–Neeman arXiv record, last revised May 2022) calls it open, and Wikipedia's list still carries the bullet unchanged. The one pre-window paper that addresses this question directly (Moore, Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 2021) could not be read in full, so its two results are unknown to me.
problem_asks: One question: is ZFC together with OCA and 2^ℵ0 > ℵ2 consistent? Parts: (1) OCA, the axiom the bullet names. The bullet links the Wikipedia article 'Open coloring axiom', whose statement section is Todorcevic's form: every open graph on a separable metrizable space (for the article, a set of reals) either has countable chromatic number or contains an uncountable clique. This reading takes the bullet's 'OCA' to be that axiom (OCA_T). The Abraham–Rubin–Shelah version (OCA_ARS, colourings of pairs from ω1) is a different axiom and is not what the statement names. (2) The cardinal condition 2^ℵ0 > ℵ2, i.e. the continuum is at least ℵ3. (3) Consistency is relative to ZFC: a positive answer is a model of ZFC + OCA + 2^ℵ0 ≥ ℵ3 (typically by forcing); a negative answer is a proof that OCA forces 2^ℵ0 ≤ ℵ2. The statement does not ask for the value of the continuum in a particular model.

events.what_happened: Justin Tatch Moore, 'Open colorings, the continuum and the second uncountable cardinal', Proc. AMS 130 (2002), no. 9, 2753–2759. Shows that the conjunction of the Abraham–Rubin–Shelah formulation (OCA_ARS) and Todorcevic's formulation (OCA_T) implies 2^ℵ0 = ℵ2. I did not reach the paper itself (AMS page returned HTTP 403). Its content is taken from Gilton–Neeman's citation ('Moore has shown in [6] that OCA_T + OCA_ARS does decide that the continuum is exactly ℵ2') and from the abstract quoted in Moore's 2019 Fields Institute talk.
events.delivers: 2^ℵ0 = ℵ2 under the conjunction OCA_ARS + OCA_T. This is a conjunction with a second axiom, so it does not bound the continuum for OCA_T on its own, and it says nothing about whether OCA_T alone is consistent with 2^ℵ0 > ℵ2.
events.remains: Whether OCA_T alone forces 2^ℵ0 = ℵ2, i.e. whether OCA_T alone is consistent with 2^ℵ0 > ℵ2. Moore's own 2019 talk and Gilton–Neeman (JML 2022) both state this as open.

events.what_happened: Itay Neeman, 'Todorcevic Open Coloring Axiom for Spaces Smaller than the Continuum' (UCLA preprint OCAsmall.pdf; undated, no journal listed on Neeman's page). Per search excerpts of the abstract and introduction (the PDF did not decode for me), it shows that OCA_T restricted to spaces of size strictly less than the continuum is consistent with arbitrarily large continuum. The excerpts also say: with a Mahlo cardinal, the restricted axiom plus a Knaster-type MA is consistent with arbitrarily large continuum; the models satisfy b = ℵ2; Moore's OCA_T + OCA_ARS ⇒ c = ℵ2 argument needs only OCA_T restricted to ℵ2-sized spaces, b = ℵ2 and OCA_ARS; and the restricted axiom with b = ℵ2 is consistent with arbitrarily large continuum. The excerpts also say that the full question, whether OCA_T forces c = ℵ2, is a central open question, and that all known models of OCA_T have c = ℵ2.

events.what_happened: Lorenzo Notaro, 'Open Colorings and Baumgartner's Axiom', arXiv:2601.01166 (math.LO). Theorem 1 (per the HTML v1 text): it is consistent relative to ZF that MA_ℵ1 + OCA_T holds while Baumgartner's Axiom (BA) and OCA_ARS both fail. Theorem 5 strengthens this with a nonstationarily 2-entangled sequence. Corollary 2: in the model there is an ℵ1-dense set of reals that is neither increasing nor reversible. The model is a finite-support iteration of length ω2 over L with a diamond sequence. The paper does not state the value of 2^ℵ0 in the model. It answers a question of Farah on whether BA follows from MA_ℵ1 + OCA_T.

events.delivers: A consistency result for MA_ℵ1 + OCA_T + ¬BA (+ ¬OCA_ARS). Nothing about 2^ℵ0 or about whether OCA_T is consistent with c > ℵ2. The model's continuum is not given in the paper. A reader might infer c = ℵ2 from the ω2-length iteration, but the paper does not say so and I have not verified it.
events.remains: The whole bullet: whether OCA_T is consistent with 2^ℵ0 > ℵ2.

disputes.summary: Todorcevic first called his axiom the Open Coloring Axiom, but that name was already used by Abraham, Rubin and Shelah for their different axiom, so Todorcevic renamed his the Open Graph Axiom (OGA). The bullet's word 'OCA' is therefore ambiguous between the two. I read it as Todorcevic's form (OCA_T) because the Wikipedia article's statement and its 'follows from PFA' remark match that form. The ARS reading gives a different answer (see competing_reading).

Matos-Wiederhold (arXiv:2201.11622): the v1 abstract, as read in a search excerpt, says OCA implies b = ℵ1, which would contradict ¬CH; the v2 text says b = ℵ2 (Theorem 3.8), which matches Todorcevic and Gilton–Neeman. I read only v2 and did not verify v1.

summary: Nothing since 26 January 2024 settles or moves this bullet, and no source I found claims a resolution. Read in its Todorcevic form (OCA_T), the question as Wikipedia states it is open in every source I could read that addresses it directly. The Wikipedia list still carries the bullet ('Is OCA (the open coloring axiom) consistent with 2^ℵ0 > ℵ2?') with no progress noted, and the Wikipedia OCA article was last edited 27 May 2026. Pre-window results: Moore (PAMS 2002) proves OCA_ARS + OCA_T implies 2^ℵ0 = ℵ2, a conjunction and so not an answer for OCA_T alone; Gilton–Neeman (arXiv 2019, JML 2022) prove OCA_ARS consistent with 2^ℵ0 = ℵ3, a different axiom; Farah's unpublished note (undated, cited 2022) gives consistency of OCA_T(ℵ1) with large continuum; Matos-Wiederhold (2022, expository) shows OCA_T implies b = ℵ2, so c ≥ ℵ2 and ¬CH. Neeman's undated note (the grant number suggests post-2021; possibly inside the window, not confirmed) shows OCA_T restricted to spaces smaller than the continuum is consistent with arbitrarily large continuum, a restriction and not the full axiom. Moore (APAL 2021, online 12 Oct 2020) addresses the question directly through 'two results', which I could not read; this is the most important gap. In-window items (Notaro Jan 2026, Marun–Shelah–Switzer Dec 2025, Martinez-Ranero–Polymeris Nov 2025, Schlicht–Sziráki v4 July 2026, De Bondt–Farah–Vignati v6 Oct 2024) concern Baumgartner's Axiom, entangled Suslin lines, definable dichotomies or consequences of OCA_T, and none states the continuum for OCA_T. Close calls: (a) which axiom 'OCA' names, where I read it as OCA_T; (b) whether restricted versions (Farah's ℵ1 case, Neeman's size < c case) count as 'the question', where I say no because they restrict the axiom; (c) whether Moore 2021's two results settle the question, which I could not check. AI: I found no AI system credited with anything on this problem. Searches for AI involvement (general set-theory AI, Lean formalisations, AI disclosures in forcing papers) found nothing relevant. The one set-theory AI disclosure I saw (Goldstern–Goto, arXiv:2609.17153, 15 Sep 2026: ChatGPT for heuristic suggestions) concerns minimality in forcing and does not mention OCA. OpenAI's 1 Aug 2026 report on its internal Astra model claims ten results; secondary coverage lists none in set theory, though I could not reach the primary report.
competing_reading: (1) If 'OCA' means either version, Gilton–Neeman (2019; JML 2022) show OCA_ARS is consistent with 2^ℵ0 = ℵ3, so the answer is 'yes' for that reading. (2) If restricted versions count, Neeman (undated) and Farah (undated) show OCA_T(<c) and OCA_T(ℵ1) consistent with arbitrarily large continuum, and the answer would be 'yes' for the restriction. (3) If Moore 2021 has a result that OCA_T alone forces 2^ℵ0 = ℵ2, the answer would be 'no', and the bullet would be resolved in the negative by a 2021 result. I could not check (3), and the abstract's framing ('two results relating to' the bullet's question) leaves it open. My reading, that the bullet is about OCA_T in full and that all results so far are partial or about other axioms, is the one I think best fits the sources I could read.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Moore, 'Some remarks on the Open Coloring Axiom', APAL 172(5) (2021) 102912: what the two results are, and whether either says that OCA_T (or OCA) alone forces 2^ℵ0 = ℵ2. (2) Neeman's OCAsmall.pdf: its date, its venue, and its exact statements, in particular whether anything addresses the full OCA_T. (3) Farah's unpublished note: its location, date and exact statement. (4) The full text of the Asperó–Schindler ICM 2026 survey (ueaeprints 102315), to see whether it states the status of OCA_T. (5) A zbMATH or MathSciNet search for papers after 2024 on OCA_T and the continuum, which I could not run. (6) The full Notaro introduction, to see whether it states the value of 2^ℵ0 in its model or flags the bullet as open.
